screen15-a1.glyph: two horizontal lines, the lower one shorter
screen15-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Menu" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen15-a1.convention_relied_on: two/three stacked lines = open the main menu (hamburger) - my reading; the two-line variant is slightly less canonical than three lines
screen15-a1.initial_rationale: no label, but two stacked horizontal lines is a recognizable variant of the hamburger menu convention - common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test
screen15-a1.deciding_evidence: tapping it slid a navigation drawer in from the left, exactly what the menu convention promises; the missing label is not a barrier; tested once on screen1-a1 and carried to this identical control

screen15-a2.description: pill in the header with a sparkle glyph and the words 'Get Plus'
screen15-a2.location: pill in the header with a sparkle glyph and the words 'Get Plus'
screen15-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Get Plus" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen15-a2.initial_rationale: visible words 'Get Plus' with a sparkle; 'Plus' is a product name a first-time user has no way to decode, and nothing says it costs money
screen15-a2.deciding_evidence: tapping opened a paywall ('ChatGPT Plus', 'Upgrade for $19.99', 'Renews monthly') - a paid monthly subscription the words 'Get Plus' never mentioned; tested once on screen1-a2 and carried to this identical control
screen15-a2.recommendation: say what it is and that it is paid, e.g. 'Upgrade to Plus (paid plan)'

screen15-a3.glyph: speech bubble drawn with a broken outline
screen15-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Temporary chat" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen15-a3.initial_rationale: a speech bubble drawn with a broken outline is not an established convention and carries no label
screen15-a3.deciding_evidence: no tooltip on long-press and no visible text in any state before activation; the words 'Temporary chat' appear only on the screen the tap opens; tested once on screen1-a3 and carried to this identical control
screen15-a3.recommendation: add a visible label beside or under the glyph, e.g. 'Temporary chat (not saved)'

screen15-a4.deciding_evidence: the visible words 'Start a voice chat' state the action; not exercised because starting voice mode is outside the safety rules, and the row no longer appears on the live build; tested once on screen1-a4 and carried to this identical control

screen15-a9.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Dictation" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen15-a9.convention_relied_on: microphone = speak instead of typing - my reading
screen15-a9.initial_rationale: unlabeled microphone; microphone = speak / voice input is an established convention - exemption pending test
screen15-a9.deciding_evidence: tapping raised the system request to record audio - the microphone convention held (permission was denied per safety rules); tested once on screen1-a9 and carried to this identical control

screen15-a10.glyph: blue filled circle with vertical sound-wave bars
screen15-a10.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Start a voice conversation" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen15-a10.initial_rationale: a filled circle with vertical sound-wave bars is not an established convention a first-time user would read, and it carries no label
screen15-a10.deciding_evidence: no label in any state before the tap; only after tapping does a dialog mention 'Voice', and the control sits right beside a microphone, so the two voice controls are not told apart; tested once on screen1-a10 and carried to this identical control
screen15-a10.recommendation: label it, e.g. 'Talk with ChatGPT' beside the glyph, and distinguish it from the dictation microphone
